title: Contract-first dashboard playbook (lab notes)
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a working lab doc to try a "contract-first" approach to building operational dashboards for inference services. Instead of starting from panel ideas, we declare small, testable metric contracts (name, semantic, owners, SLO behavior) and derive dashboard panels and tracing anchors from those contracts. The aim is compact, action-oriented dashboards that make triage decisions (evict/scale/fallback) obvious.

Goals for this iteration:
- Define 6 metric contracts for token-serving stacks with concrete guardrails.
- Prototype a 2-row dashboard layout (operator + incident playbook panels).
- Add tracing span anchors and example span attributes for rapid drilldowns.
- Sketch sampling and probe schedule to keep query cost bounded.

Why contract-first?
- Reduces panel sprawl: every panel must be justified by a contract (owner, permissible drift, alert trigger).
- Enables automated regression tests: metric contract is the input to CI fuzz tests and synthetic probes.
- Makes runbooks deterministic: when a contract violates, the runbook points to one canonical panel + trace anchor.

Metric contracts (short form):
1) session-first-token-latency_ms
   - semantic: p95 server-side latency from request receive -> last token emitted (server time only).
   - unit: ms, aggregation: p50/p90/p95/p99, cardinality: model, region, tenancy-tier.
   - owner: serving-runtime/latency-team (Marco Liu)
   - alert: p95 > 420ms for 5m AND traffic-weighted p95 increase > 20% vs baseline
   - permitted drift: < 10% sustained month-over-month

2) kv-cache-warmth_ratio
   - semantic: fraction of requests hitting warm KV cache (prefix or session cache) at first token generation.
   - unit: ratio 0..1, aggregation: rate over 1m/5m, cardinality: model-version, tenant-id-class (top-100 tenants), region.
   - owner: runtime-cache-team (Renee Thompson)
   - alert: absolute < 0.4 for an enterprise model + concurrent increase in token-latency > 15%

3) token-cost-per-req_usd
   - semantic: estimated incremental infra cost per request (amortized tokens + kernel cost).
   - unit: USD, aggregation: mean, percentile, cardinality: route/model/config.
   - owner: infra-cost (Samir Das)
   - alert: mean > expected by 30% for > 1h OR cost-per-token spike aligned with model rollout

4) partial-response-rate
   - semantic: fraction of requests that ended with last_token_missing or truncated by resource limit (not client cancel).
   - unit: ratio, aggregation: 1m/5m, cardinality: route/model.
   - owner: product-hosted-api (Aisha Patel)
   - alert: absolute > 0.02 AND correlated with client error-rate increase

5) trace-anchored-hallucination-signal
   - semantic: operator-annotated metric derived from sampling (human review) about hallucination-like outputs for a small probe set.
   - unit: fraction-of-samples-flagged, aggregation: daily/weekly, cardinality: model/version.
   - owner: applied-ml/evals (TBD)
   - alert: week-over-week increase > 50% for a model-version under rollout

6) operator-queue-depth
   - semantic: backpressure queue for operator work (e.g., post-token expensive ops like rerank, tool-call orchestration).
   - unit: integer, aggregation: max/avg, cardinality: worker-pool, tenant-class.
   - owner: platform-engineering
   - alert: sustained > 75% of worker capacity for 10m

Dashboard layout (sketch):
Row A (Operator quick triage):
- Panel 1: p95 session-first-token-latency (split by model-version) with anomaly shading and recent deploy markers.
- Panel 2: kv-cache-warmth_ratio trend with tenant-weighted sparkline and top 5 tenants by drop. Click to open tenant session replay.
- Panel 3: operator-queue-depth heatmap across worker pools + capacity annotation.
- Panel 4: live synthetic probe status (last-run result per probe), includes next-run ETA.
Row B (Incident playbook and context):
- Panel 5: token-cost-per-req_usd trend with recent config changes overlay.
- Panel 6: partial-response-rate + example truncated request ids (linked to logs) for fast replay.
- Panel 7: trace sample waterfall anchored to the p95 spike window (links to span ids).
- Panel 8: continuous eval signal (trace-anchored-hallucination-signal) and recent flagged examples.

Tracing anchors and span attributes (practical):
- Anchor name: token-emitter-span; recommended attributes: model.name, model.version, tenant.id_class, kv.cache_hit (bool), kv.latency_ms, operator.queue_wait_ms, executor.gpu_id, request.seed_id
- Anchor name: prefill-span (if batching): attributes: batch.size, batch.wait_ms, batch.policy_id
- Sampling: adopt severity-weighted adaptive sampling: always-sample error spans and p95+ latency traces; sample 1% of normal requests but upweight by tenant and model revenue class.
- Trace correlation: include request.trace_id in all logs and metric point tags for easy join (session_id, trace_id, request_timeline_id).

Probe schedule and cost guardrails:
- Micro-probes: 1k lightweight probes per region per hour (checks prefix warmth, cold start latency)
- Session probes: 50 tenant-focused session replays per hour (top tenants + rotating long-tail)
- Synthetic evals: daily full-eval run for top models (costly, scheduled off-peak)
- Query cost cap: throttle synthetic evals above $X/day (TODO set exact amount), alert if synthetic consumes > 20% of query budget for the environment

Runbook snippets (when p95 latency breach):
1) Confirm if breach spans all models or a single model-version (Panel 1 split).
2) Check kv-cache-warmth_ratio drop in same timeframe. If yes, run cache-warmth remediation: restart prefetch workers for affected workers (owner: runtime-cache).
3) If warmth stable, inspect operator-queue-depth heatmap. If queue backpressure present, consider autoscale worker pool or fallback to low-cost variant.
4) If none above, dig into trace waterfall for prefill / kernel hotspots and escalate to serving-runtime. Attach candidate PRs/commits between t-15m and t0.

Operational practices and automation ideas:
- Metric contract registry: store contracts as YAML checked into github.com/redwood-inference/metric-contracts. Contracts generate dashboard templates and alert rules automatically.
- CI synthetic guard: any model rollout PR must include a smoke probe run that exercises the contract tests and posts results to the PR.
- Trace anchors indicated in the contract produce an auto-link in the dashboard panel linking to trace explorer with prefilled query.

Unresolved questions / open items:
- How do we define tenant.id_class boundaries for cardinality without exploding series? Proposal: top-100 weighted tenants + coarse buckets for the rest (enterprise/smb/startup).
- Synthetic cost budget numbers (Samir to propose a monthly cap).
- Who owns the hallucination sampling pipeline to make trace-anchored-hallucination-signal operational? Need applied-ml lead.
- Contract storage format: YAML vs. proto? Prefer YAML for editability but need schema validation.

Next steps (short horizon):
- [ ] Convert these 6 metric contracts into the repo YAML schema (owner: Aisha) — target 2026-03-05
- [ ] Prototype dashboard JSON from contract generator for a single region and model (owner: Marco) — target 2026-03-10
- [ ] Wire the trace anchor links for panel 7 using the trace explorer deep link spec (owner: Renee) — target 2026-03-12
- [ ] Budget proposal for synthetic probes and evals (owner: Samir) — target 2026-03-08

Quick notes / scratchroom (informal):
- Thinking: when kv-warmth drops for a small subset of high-value tenants, we might auto-fallback them to dedicated cache pools — need cost model.
- Idea: panel drilldown should show "likely next action" buttons (scale, restart prefetch, fallback) that open a prescriptive runbook with a prefilled Incident Slack thread template.
- Slack refs: #obs-ops, #deployments, thread from 2026-02-17: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C0ABC12345/p1676600000000
